name: Huerta de San Vicente (García Lorca house-museum), Granada
story: The García Lorca family's summer home from 1926 to 1936, where the poet wrote much of Blood Wedding and Yerma. Lorca came here from Madrid in July 1936, days before the rising. When the military seized Granada, the house was searched; his brother-in-law Manuel Fernández-Montesinos, the Socialist mayor, was arrested and shot in August. Lorca took refuge in the house of the Rosales family, Falangists and friends, but was arrested there on 16 August and killed days later near Alfacar. The family sold the house to the city in 1985 and it opened as a museum in 1995. It is the best place to understand Lorca the writer before visiting the sites of his death.
see: The whitewashed farmhouse, largely unchanged, with family furniture, Lorca's desk and piano, drawings and documents, in the Parque García Lorca.
plan: Guided visits only, in small groups; closed Mondays. Book ahead in summer; small fee (free day weekly). Official site: huertadesanvicente.com.
